findings.text: User stack unwinding uses a small family of records. One trace record pairs a count with a pointer to collected addresses. One per-frame record carries signed offsets for canonical address and return and frame locations plus a flag selecting frame-pointer interpretation. One walker record carries address-sized instruction, stack and frame positions, a window size, current and available type masks, and topmost and done flags. Type selection distinguishes an empty start value from a frame-pointer mode derived from bit zero.
SuperSpeed Plus signaling rate vocabulary distinguishes four labels: one unknown value followed by three lane-count encodings covering two-by-one, one-by-two and two-by-two arrangements.

EHCI debug port mailbox is five consecutive host words for control, token PIDs, two data payload words and device endpoint addressing. Control packs ownership, enabled, completed, in-use, error, go, direction and length fields. PID word packs get and set token halves. Address word packs device and endpoint numbers.

Debug-port reset and external-startup helpers are fixed-result shims. The Xen variants always report the same prep outcome and the same startup failure, and the generic wrappers simply forward to those Xen variants without inspecting controller state.

EHCI capability block starts with a combined length and version word, then structural and capability parameter words, then eight routing bytes. Structural parameters encode debug-port index, indicator support, companion counts, ports per companion, routing mode, power control and port count. Capability parameters encode periodic list size support, per-port events, link power management, prefetch modes, extended capability offset, isochronous caching, park support, programmable frame length and 64-bit addressing.

EHCI operational register file lays out command then status then interrupt enable then frame index, segment, periodic base and async next, followed by tuning, configuration flag, per-port status array overlapping a device-mode variant, host extensions overlapping a vendor instruction area, and a mode-extension word. Port count is bounded by a fifteen-entry maximum.

EHCI command vocabulary controls resume duration, per-port event enable, prefetch enables, park enable and park count, partial reset, async doorbell, async and periodic enables, controller reset and run. Status vocabulary reports per-port events, schedule states, reclamation, halt, async advance, fatal, rollover, port change, error and normal completion, with the low completion group also serving as interrupt enables.

EHCI per-port status packs device address, suspend status, wake enables for overcurrent and disconnect and connect, test selection, LED selection, companion ownership, power, link speed, link power state, reset, suspend, resume, overcurrent and enable change pairs, and connect change pair. Only connect, enable and overcurrent changes are write-clear. Suspend handshake distinguishes acknowledge, negative acknowledge, stall and error outcomes.

EHCI mode words select stream disable, endian choice and host versus idle roles. Two host-side PHY extensions report clock disable and detected port speed. A mode-extension word adds bus power selection plus host role selection.
Early xHCI debug console setup is a build-time unavailable stub: hardware setup always reports device absence and console registration performs no action.

User-return notification has two build variants. The active variant links a callback invoked on return to user with an intrusive hash linkage. The inactive variant is an empty placeholder with no members and all operations become no-ops.

Return-to-user pending state moves with scheduling: when the outgoing task carries the pending marker, that marker is cleared from it and set on the incoming task. A separate clear operation drops the marker from a given task. In the inactive build both transitions do nothing.

User-events memory tracking links a memory descriptor owner into a global list and owns a list of enablers, with back pointers to the address space and to a one-shot successor, two reference-style counts for lifetime and attached tasks, and deferred release work.

User-events lifetime follows process lifecycle. Fork with shared address space shares the tracker and accounts one more task; fork without shared address space duplicates tracking for the child; exec and exit detach tracking from the affected task. All three hooks ignore absent tasks or absent trackers, and the disabled build provides empty hooks.

Generic helpers expose a condition-gated loop prefix that skips its body when the condition is false, a conditional pointer selector returning either a pointer or null, and an address-range test checking whether a pointer lies inside a given object using address arithmetic and object size.

Nearest-value search over an ordered table compares the query against midpoints between neighbors and selects the nearer neighbor on ties favoring the farther side in the scanned direction. One form scans upward for ascending tables and the other scans downward for descending tables, both returning an index and leaving edge queries clamped by scan bounds.

Default identity strings name the system, a configurable default host name source, and a placeholder domain value. A small enumeration selects which identity field a proc notification refers to, covering architecture, type, release, version, host and domain.
UTS namespace record bundles a host identity block, owning user namespace, resource counter block and generic namespace linkage, with layout randomization requested.

UTS namespace handles convert from generic linkage via container offset, acquire with a namespace reference increment, and release with a put that frees only when the last reference drops. The disabled build makes acquire and release empty, rejects creation of a new UTS view with an invalid-argument error while otherwise returning the old namespace, and provides an empty subsystem initializer.

Callers obtain the current host identity through the current task namespace proxy and obtain the initial identity through the initial namespace object. Proc change notification is an empty hook in these fragments.

GUID and UUID are each sixteen raw bytes in fixed array wrappers. Two initializer forms differ only in byte order of the first three numeric fields: one stores them least-significant first and the other most-significant first, while the trailing eight bytes keep input order in both.
Binary identifier width is sixteen bytes and canonical textual length is thirty-six characters.

GUID and UUID helpers provide equality by full-width memory comparison, copy and import and export by full-width memory move between objects and byte buffers, and null tests by comparison against global null values.

Virtual data path queue support uses a callback record pairing a function and opaque datum with an event trigger, an address-plus-length notification mapping, and queue progress unions with split and packed layouts. Split progress tracks an available index; packed progress tracks counters plus indices for available and used sides using narrow bit fields.

Virtual data path device record embeds a generic device, address-mapping state, configuration and mapping operation tables, a configuration lock, an index, feature-valid and address-mode flags, queue and group and address-space counts, and a management parent. Related records describe an inclusive I/O address interval, a device configuration update carrying features plus network identity fields and a validity mask, and a file-backed mapping with file and offset.
Device configuration reads and updates are serialized by a per-device read-write semaphore held across get and set configuration operations.

EHCI capability length and version decoding depends on controller endian mode, so using the wrong byte order mislocates all operational registers. Port status contains mixed write-one-to-clear and read-write fields, so read-modify-write without masking can accidentally clear change indications.
